cards.name: Yellow Sun Rays Left Bright
cards.summary: Lens Flare effect preset (Effects > Camera > Lens Flare). The effect draws up to five light elements: the flare (brightest core), a halo ring, a reflection tail of small circles, rays, and an anamorphic light streak; a preset stores a combination of these. By name, the brighter version of Yellow Sun Rays Left: a stronger golden sun with rays from the left (unverified).
use_for: strong golden backlight on a hero image
bright summer or festival posters
sky-heavy photos that can carry a big flare
avoid: Mid-tone photos: the bright variant can blow out detail around the centre; try the plain Yellow Sun Rays Left first.
Light, busy or already glaring photos: the flare washes out and reads as haze; it works best over a darker area of the picture.

The look is unverified: the 2026-10-13 render of this preset's values was identical to 5 other preset(s), because colour (Red / Yellow / Blue) and the flare position (Left / Right) cannot be sent by script; the card is written from the name, so apply it once in the dialog and check by eye.
cards.applies_to: a bitmap (the harvest lists requires: bitmap); the scripted route Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect needs a bitmap shape, while from Effects > Camera > Lens Flare CorelDRAW 2024 also applies it to a vector object as a non-destructive effect (Lens Flare effect harvest)
cards.how_to_apply: Select a bitmap (or any object when working from the menu), choose Effects > Camera > Lens Flare, then pick 'Yellow Sun Rays Left Bright' from the dialog's Preset list and adjust the flare, halo, ray and reflection settings; CorelDRAW 2024 keeps the effect in the object's effect stack (Properties docker, Effects section), where it stays editable. Preset id e36d4762-1cc0-400d-94dd-2315722bd33a. Script: the effect has no preset key (a 'Preset=<guid>' token changes nothing: that is why the first gallery run gave identical renders). verified.note: Not rendered: the 2026-10-13 live chain sent this preset's values as explicit keys, but the render was pixel-identical to 5 other preset(s) sent with the same command, so it was dropped; what tells them apart is colour (Red / Yellow / Blue) and the flare position (Left / Right), which ApplyBitmapEffect cannot carry. Harness limit, not a verdict on the preset: its look is untested.
